<reason>A occupied the motion with a consistent bright line: researcher value, even independently certified, cannot keep the body. B’s presumption-plus-exception was serious, but A showed incomplete colonial records are ordinary, so “necessity” and hearings still mean possession and postponed burial. B landed the hard case of otherwise-lost abuse evidence and descendant disagreement; A answered it directly and made the remaining choice easier to vote.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s first rebuttal that B’s “substantial need” test matches the ordinary condition of these collections, so a hearing is still a research veto and “every cemetery already forecloses sampling.”</best_rebuttal>
